info.description:
The DMS answers three kinds of caller, and never more than the caller's own rights allow.

* **A person on the page** - Windows authentication (IIS). The DMS asks AD what that person may see, folder
  by folder, and answers nothing else. Most endpoints are these.
* **A page of the repository** - a dashboard or a KPI page runs sandboxed, with an origin of its own, so it
  cannot sign in. It is given a page key when it is opened (`?t=`), good for the folder it was opened from
  and for a few hours. Reading only.
* **An application** - a key of its own (`X-DMS-Api-Key`, or `Authorization: Bearer`). The key names what it
  may read and the AD account it acts as: the DMS answers it exactly what that account may see. One
  endpoint writes (the KPI Builder's), the rest read.

The DMS writes on the file server with its own account, so an approver needs no rights there at all - but it
never stands in for a right the person does not have. See `docs/13-Machine-API.md` for applications,
`docs/15-KPI-Builder-Contract.md` for the KPI Builder and `docs/14-API-Reference.md` for the whole list.
info.title: RH DMS Web API

of it is out in SharePoint. Open it in the browser:

post.description:
An approver edits the document on their own PC and attaches it here as their remarks. The submitted
file is never touched: the attachment is kept beside the document, named after the approver, so several
approvers can send remarks without overwriting each other and the approved revision stays as it was.

post.description:
Rename the file of a document in Working (owner or super user). The register follows: working path,
title (when it was the file name) and draft revision (from a _RevNN in the new name).

Start the next revision of an approved document, on the same record: from a copy of the
approved version, or from a file uploaded from the user's PC. The draft is saved next to the
document as <name>_RevNN_DRAFT.<ext>; on approval the file service makes it the current version
and moves the previous one to Obsolete_ReadOnly.

Share approved revisions with a customer: the files are copied straight into the customer folder on the
Large File Exchange site (<library>/Outbound/<Customer>/, the name of the folder under 02_Customers) and
SharePoint invites the person to that folder (view only, B2B guest). More documents can go in the same
share; every later share adds to the same folder. A OneDrive shortcut DMS_<Customer> is added for the
user. Only approved documents, by the owner or a DMS super user; one Control Audit row per document.

get.description:

post.description:
Send a registered document for approval: it moves to Submitted, the approvers are told, and the
file goes to the Submitted folder.

Take a submitted document back to Working (owner or super user). The approval cycle ends,
the file service returns the file to its place, and it can be submitted again.

get.description: What is on the Large File Exchange site now for this customer / person (read only, for the Share dialog).

post.description:
Run the file moves now: every approved document goes to Current_ReadOnly in its own folder (the
previous revision to Obsolete_ReadOnly), read only, with its SHA-256 in the record. A super user can
run it whenever they like, also when the DMS does not run it on a timer (DMS_FILE_SERVICE_SECONDS).
Done editing: the DMS writes what the person changed back to the file server and removes the copy.

Open this file in SharePoint, with the person's own Microsoft account: the DMS (the only account with
rights on the file server) puts a copy there and gives that one person edit, or read only when the
document is released. A released (read-only) document is never opened for editing.

and it may not read the DMS's cookies or call the DMS as the person looking at it, because a page
that arrives from a shared folder is not trusted with their account.

The file itself, for someone AD lets read it. The DMS reads it with its own account: an approver
needs no rights on the file server.

A link to this file or folder that means something only inside the DMS: a short token, not the path

and what the person may see is decided there, by their own AD groups, as always.

get.description:
The Markdown of every approved document, as it lies in the Current_ReadOnly folders.

Four things per file: the document's id, its name, its revision and where the Markdown is. This is
the AI's list - it reads these files - so it is taken from the folders themselves and not only from
the register: a document released by hand is in Current_ReadOnly with its Markdown beside it, and the
AI should read that too. What the register knows fills in the id and the revision; what it does not
know is read from the Markdown's own first lines, which the DMS wrote when it made the file.

The departments of the company: the folders under General, with the name the page shows and the

For an application, not for a person. AD decides here as everywhere: a department the key's account
may not see is not in the answer.

Every approved document the DMS holds, with the file that is in force and the Markdown beside it.

This is what the company's AI reads from: it asks the DMS which documents are approved and where
their files are, instead of being pointed at a folder and left to guess what in it is current. A
revision that has been replaced is not here; nor is anything still in work.

post.description:
The KPI Builder publishes one KPI of one department: its page and the data behind it, together.

    POST /api/v1/kpi/publish   department=Production  kpi=Yield
                               files=@Yield.html  files=@Yield.json

What it makes, under that department's KPIs folder:

    KPIs\Yield\Yield.html                      the page, writable - the next build replaces it
    KPIs\Yield\Current_ReadOnly\Yield.json    the data, released: read only, in the register

One KPI, one folder named after it, made on the first publish - and the KPIs folder itself made if
the department has none yet. A page named dashboard_<something>.html is the department's dashboard
rather than one KPI: it stays at the root of KPIs and its data is released into the KPIs folder's
own Current_ReadOnly, which is where a dashboard layout belongs.

The application acts as its AD account: that account needs Modify there, as a person would.

get.description: The DMS page itself: one HTML file, served to the signed-in browser.

The tab's icon: the logo on a white square that it fills, the shape a tab icon is drawn in. The wide
logo itself is shrunk into a corner of the tab instead. Without any icon the browser shows whatever it
likes - often the icon of the site that tab held before.
The company logo: put logo.png in dms_api/static (a drawn "rh" is shown without it).

A page of the DMS's own, served exactly as any HTML in the repository is: into the sandbox, with a
key in its address and the bridge in front of it. It then asks the DMS three things and says what came
back. If this page works and yours does not, the fault is in the page; if this one fails, it says
which of the three steps failed and that is the DMS's side to fix.
